full.description: This is a high-power photomicrograph of a bone marrow biopsy section stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image displays hypercellular bone marrow packed with numerous atypical plasma cells, showing immature nuclear features. These findings are characteristic of multiple myeloma, a hematologic malignancy characterized by the clonal proliferation of plasma cells within the bone marrow.

blind.description: This is a microscopic image of subcutaneous adipose tissue showing features of panniculitis. There is an infiltration of atypical lymphoid cells closely apposed to the surface of individual fat cells, forming characteristic ring-like structures around them. Focal phagocytosis of the lymphoid cells is also visible within the infiltrate. These findings are most consistent with subcutaneous panniculitic T-cell lymphoma.

random.description: This image is a photomicrograph of bone marrow tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows hypercellular marrow with a prominent focus of inflammation, characterized by an aggregate of inflammatory cells and histiocytes. The findings are indicative of an inflammatory process or granulomatous lesion within the bone marrow.
